record.original_question: Can every complex surface be embedded as a subdomain of a disk-convex complex surface?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 Can every complex surface be imbedded as a subdomain into a disk-convex complex surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complex surface is a connected complex manifold of complex dimension 2. A complex manifold X is called disk-convex if for every compact subset K ⊂ X there exists a compact subset K' ⊂ X such that every holomorphic map f : \overline{\mathbb{D}} \to X from the closed unit disk in ℂ which sends the boundary circle ∂\mathbb{D} into K must send the entire closed disk \overline{\mathbb{D}} into K'. By a subdomain of a complex surface Y we mean an open connected subset of Y endowed with the induced complex structure.

Question: Does every complex surface X admit a holomorphic embedding onto a subdomain of some disk-convex complex surface Y?
